messages:
alice_support: FYI customer reported rerank returning identical scores and our console cURL example seems to break when they paste it into Windows CMD. They pasted from Console -> Copy cURL.
ben_docs: ugh, this is the classic single-quote vs double-quote thing on Windows. Do we show single quotes in the Console snippet for the rerank example?
alice_support: Console shows something like:
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": {"queries": ["best hotels in SF"], "candidates": ["Hotel A\nHotel B"]}}'
```
Customer pasted and got a 400, then tried double quotes but CMD treated nested quotes weird and the body got truncated.
cara_eng: Also saw that if candidates are newline-separated in a single string sometimes our parser splits badly and returns low-quality scores (or identical defaults). Could be the body structure our client lib expects is arrays, not newline strings.
eva_support: Customer sent full example. When they passed candidates as a single newline string we returned scores all 0.5. When they switched to ["Hotel A","Hotel B"] they got meaningful scores.
ben_docs: That's important. Our docs show the console with an inline JSON blob which uses single quotes to avoid escaping double quotes, but that is not cross-shell portable. We should display both variants and explicitly call out Windows CMD + PowerShell differences.
cara_eng: Repro steps I used (Linux/Mac):
1) curl with JSON body as array -> works
2) curl with candidates as single string with embedded \n -> our backend splits on "\n" and then normalizes whitespace; if the client didn't actually send a literal backslash-n but a real newline inside the JSON string we treat it as one candidate including newline and that triggers a normalization path that collapses tokens leading to similar embeddings -> similar scores.
ben_docs: Oof. So two messy things: console cURL quoting and ambiguous candidate formatting. We should change Console to generate a -d @- form or a file-like example for Windows, and add a note: use JSON arrays for candidates or explicit \n escape sequences.
alice_support: Customer wants a quick patch they can paste. Can we give them a Windows-safe cURL snippet and mention PowerShell's single-quote vs double-quote behavior?
cara_eng: Suggested Windows CMD example:
```
curl "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" ^
  -H "Authorization: Bearer %REDWOOD_KEY%" ^
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" ^
  -d "{\"input\":{\"queries\":[\"best hotels in SF\"],\"candidates\":[\"Hotel A\",\"Hotel B\"]}}"
```
And PowerShell example:
```
curl "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" `
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $env:REDWOOD_KEY' `
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' `
  -Body '{"input":{"queries":["best hotels in SF"],"candidates":["Hotel A","Hotel B"]}}' -Method Post
```
(Yes, PowerShell has -Body and different quoting.)
eva_support: I pasted the Windows CMD example to the customer and they confirmed it worked. They also said the Console copy still gives the single-quote style by default though.
ben_docs: Plan: update Console to provide a shell selector (bash/powershell/cmd) and generate appropriate quoting per shell. Short-term: add a banner in rerank docs: "Prefer JSON arrays for candidates; avoid embedding raw newlines in a single candidate string. On Windows use double quotes and escape inner quotes as shown." I'll open a docs PR.
cara_eng: I'll add a defensive parse check: if we see a single string with embedded newlines in candidates, treat it as newline-separated list and log a warning in the response metadata so support can point customers to the warning. Also add a scoring regression test: identical inputs should not produce identical scores unless semantics match.
deploy-bot: deploy requested by cara_eng: rerank-parse-warn -> queued for canary
alice_support: Thanks all. I'll update the customer thread with the Windows CMD and PowerShell snippets, and ask them to retry with explicit JSON arrays. Closing here after confirmation. :thumbsup:
